prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
competitors_mentioned: Do Not Give a Recorded Statement
answer_verbatim:
I can help you pick the right lawyer — first, a few quick questions so I can give specific recommendations:
- When did the accident happen?
- Where exactly in Pleasanton (intersection/highway)?
- Were there injuries? How serious (treatment, hospital stay, ongoing care)?
- Were you the driver, passenger, pedestrian, cyclist?
- Is fault disputed? Were police or witnesses involved?
- Has any insurance company contacted you or made a settlement offer?
- Do you already have medical bills or unpaid liens?
- Do you prefer a local Pleasanton/Tri‑Valley lawyer or are you open to firms in Oakland, Walnut Creek, Fremont, etc.?

If you want immediate general guidance, here’s what to look for and what to do next.

Which type of lawyer
- You want a California personal-injury attorney who handles auto collisions (often called car-accident attorneys). If there are catastrophic injuries or long-term disability, look for lawyers experienced with severe-injury or wrongful-death cases.

How to choose — key criteria
- Relevant experience: regular handling of car-accident cases and trial experience (many cases settle; you want someone who can and will take the case to trial if needed).
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Alameda County courts, local pipeline of expert witnesses, and local insurers.
- Track record: settlements/verdicts in similar cases (ask for examples).
- Communication: clear explanation of strategy, regular updates, reachable staff.
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (common: ~33% if settled before suit, ~33–40% if after filing; confirm percentages and who pays costs). Ask about expenses, liens, and subrogation.
- Resources: firm should have resources to advance costs for medical records, expert reports, etc.
- Client reviews and disciplinary history: check CA State Bar and reviews on Google/Avvo/Martindale/SuperLawyers.

What to do immediately (before hiring)
- Seek and keep medical treatment — document everything.
- Preserve evidence: photos of damage, injuries, scene; witness contact info; dashcam; repair estimates.
- Do NOT give a recorded statement or sign releases for the other party’s insurer without checking a lawyer first.
- Keep a log of symptoms, missed work, and expenses.
- Note deadlines: California statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the accident (3 years for property damage). If a government vehicle was involved, different notice rules apply (much shorter). Don’t delay.

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How many car-accident cases do you handle per year? How many go to trial?
- Have you handled cases like mine (injury type, fault details)?
- What is your contingency fee and what costs would I be responsible for?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?
- What results have you obtained for similar claims?
- How long do you expect my case to take?
- Can you provide references or client testimonials?
- Are there any potential liens (medical providers, insurers) I should expect?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific outcome or dollar amount.
- Pressure to sign immediately without reviewing terms.
- Poor communication or evasive answers about experience/costs.
- No written fee agreement or unclear cost allocation.

How I can help next
- If you give me the details I asked for above, I can (a) suggest a shortlist of traits to prioritize for your situation and (b) draft messages or a script to contact attorneys for consultations. If you want, I can also outline what a reasonable settlement range might be based on your injuries and facts (not a guarantee, but a ballpark) once I have details.

If you want immediate lawyer names, tell me the specifics above and whether you prefer a small local firm or a larger regional one, and I’ll help you make a shortlist and sample questions to ask.
